f1.quote: Introduce a controlled compositional modification by substituting one constituent atom with an alternative element of similar valence but with a closer atomic mass and size to the alloy average.

f3.quote: Superconducting behavior (Tc, superconducting transition width, and residual resistivity) should be measured via resistivity and magnetic susceptibility (or specific heat) as functions of temperature under identical conditions for baseline and modified samples.

f4.quote: Reducing the variance in local lattice strain (and hence narrowing the phonon density‐of‐states distribution) via a controlled substitution will enhance Tc relative to the unmodified baseline.

f7.quote: The controlled substitution designed to reduce local lattice distortions is predicted to yield a modified alloy exhibiting a higher superconducting transition temperature and a sharper resistive and magnetic transition (lower transition width) compared to the original alloy baseline.
